reconcile.note: Clarke concedes the name Yahweh long predates Abraham but argues the patriarchs knew the word without grasping what it truly signified.

discrepancy.note: Spinoza treats the naming at Moriah as the historian's own editorial voice, distinct from the words he attributes to Abraham himself.

quotes.text: That is by the historian, not by Abraham, for he says that the place now called "In the mount of the Lord it shall be revealed," was called by Abraham, "the Lord shall provide."
quotes.attr: Benedict de Spinoza (d. 1677), A Theologico-Political Treatise, Part II (1883 trans.), ch. VIII, Endnote 9, on Genesis 22:14.

sides.snippet: Abraham called the name of that place Yahweh-Jireh.
sides.verseText: Abraham called the name of that place Yahweh-Jireh. As it is said to this day, \"In Yahweh's mountain it will be provided.

sides.snippet: by my name Yahweh I was not known to them.
sides.verseText: and I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, as God Almighty; but by my name Yahweh I was not known to them.
